others.route: Artistic work permit (Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals, art. 10)

note: Taiwan: an employer must apply to the Ministry of Labor for an employment permit before employing a foreign worker, and religious, artistic and performing art work is among the categories a foreigner may be hired for (Employment Service Act arts. 46(1)(6) and 48, amended 20 January 2025). The Act names no days of such work without the permit. Residents of the Mainland, Hong Kong and Macao come under separate acts of their own, not read; the game gives them this rule. Route corrected 2026-11-01 from the permit research (papers.permits.TW): it was “Employment permit (religious, artistic and performing art work)”.

sources.title: Laws & Regulations Database of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Employment Service Act (amended 2025-01-20)
sources.said: Employers hiring foreign nationals to work in the Republic of China are limited to the following categories, unless otherwise stipulated in the Act: ... 6.Religious, artistic, and performing art related work. ... Employers must apply to the Central Competent Authority for an employment permit before employing a foreign worker, submitting all relevant documents.

sources.title: Laws & Regulations Database of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals (amended 2025-09-24), art. 10
sources.said: A foreign professional who works as an artist may apply directly to the Ministry of Labor for a permit to engage in artistic work in the State. Such a work permit shall be for a maximum term of three years, and when necessary, an application for extension may be made for up to three years each time.
